theme: The voice of the LORD, Revelation’s thunders
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 29. The psalm is built around the phrase “the voice of the LORD,” repeated seven times. Read it aloud and listen for the sound of a storm moving across the land.
settingTheScene: Psalm 29 is a psalm of David describing a thunderstorm that sweeps in from the Mediterranean, crosses the mountains of Lebanon, and moves down to the wilderness of Kadesh in the south. It was probably used in worship at the temple. Canaanite religion said that Baal, the storm god, ruled the thunder. This psalm declares that the thunder is the voice of the LORD, and only he is the God of glory. It stands next to Revelation’s thunders and the heavenly worship of chapters 4 and 5.
observation: “Ascribe to the LORD, O heavenly beings, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength” (v. 1).
“Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness” (v. 2).
“The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders” (v. 3).
“The voice of the LORD is powerful; the voice of the LORD is full of majesty” (v. 4).
“The voice of the LORD breaks the cedars” (v. 5).
“The LORD sits enthroned over the flood; the LORD sits enthroned as king forever” (v. 10).
“May the LORD give strength to his people! May the LORD bless his people with peace!” (v. 11).
interpretation:
The psalm begins in heaven: “Ascribe to the LORD, O heavenly beings, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength. Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name; worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness.” Even the angels are called to give God the glory that belongs to him. The word “ascribe” means to give him what is already his.

Then seven times we hear the voice of the LORD. His voice is “over the waters,” that is, over the sea and the storm clouds. It “is powerful” and “full of majesty.” It “breaks the cedars,” the greatest trees of the ancient world. It makes Lebanon and Sirion (Mount Hermon) “skip like a calf, and Sirion like a young wild ox.” The mountains jump at his voice. It “flashes forth flames of fire,” meaning lightning, and it “shakes the wilderness.” The voice “makes the deer give birth and strips the forests bare.” Everything in creation trembles. And in the middle of the storm, “in his temple all cry, Glory!” Only in the temple do people understand what the thunder means: God is speaking.

The first half is about the voice of the LORD in nature, and the last is about the LORD enthroned: “The LORD sits enthroned over the flood; the LORD sits enthroned as king forever.” The flood recalls Noah, and the chaos waters of creation. God is not threatened by floods; he sits above them. He is king forever.

The last verse is the application: “May the LORD give strength to his people! May the LORD bless his people with peace!” The God whose voice shakes the mountains is the God who gives his people strength and peace. Power is not a threat to those who belong to him; it is their shelter.

In Revelation, the same imagery is used. From the throne come “flashes of lightning, and rumblings and peals of thunder” (4:5). Seven thunders speak in 10:3-4. In 19:6, the great multitude hears “the sound of many waters and like the sound of mighty peals of thunder, crying out, Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns.” In Christ, the voice of God has come in its fullest form. Hebrews 12:26 says that his voice shook the earth then, and will shake not only the earth but also the heavens.
connection: Exodus 19:16-19 and 20:18-19 describe the voice of God at Sinai. Job 37:2-5 and 38:1 describe God’s thunder. Psalm 18:13-15 and 77:18 also describe thunder. 1 Chronicles 16:28-29 echoes the call to ascribe glory. Genesis 6-9 is the flood. Psalm 93:3-4 and 104:7 also speak of the waters. Revelation 4:5, 8:5, 10:3-4, and 19:6 mention thunder. Hebrews 12:25-28 says God’s voice shakes heaven and earth. John 12:28-29 records a voice from heaven that some took for thunder. Numbers 6:24-26 pronounces blessing with peace.
application:
Next time you hear thunder, pause and say verse 3 and 10. The God who thunders is your Father.

Practice “ascribing” today: give God the glory when something goes well, instead of keeping it.

Pray verse 11 for your church and family.
prayerPrompts: Ascribe glory and strength to God, in your own words.
Worship him in the splendor of holiness.
Ask him to give you his peace.
